'''Carl Adam Petri''' (12 July 1926 in [[Leipzig]] – 2 July 2010 in [[Siegburg]])<ref name="smith15">{{cite book| first=Einar | last=Smith | title=Carl Adam Petri: Life and Science | publisher=Springer | isbn=978-3-662-48092-2 | date=2015 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof. Dr. Carl Adam Petri|url=https://www.informatik.uni-hamburg.de/TGI/mitarbeiter/profs/petri_eng.html|access-date=2020-10-25|website=www.informatik.uni-hamburg.de}}</ref> was a German [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]].

==Life and work==
[[File:Petri net example.svg|thumb|Petri net example]]
Petri created his major scientific contribution, the concept of the [[Petri net]], in 1939 at the age of 13, for the purpose of describing chemical processes.<ref>[http://www.scholarpedia.org/article/Petri_net] Carl Adam Petri and Wolfgang Reisig (2008), Scholarpedia, 3(4):6477, retrieved 2016-02-24.</ref> In 1941, his father told him about [[Konrad Zuse]]'s work on computing machines, and Carl Adam started building his own [[analog computer]].

After earning his [[Abitur]] at [[Thomasschule zu Leipzig|Thomasschule]] in 1944, he was drafted into the [[Wehrmacht]]. He was taken into British captivity until 1949, when he departed England.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last1=Reisig|first1=Wolfgang|last2=Rozenberg|first2=Grzegorz|last3=Thiagarajan|first3=P. S.|title=Transactions on Petri Nets and Other Models of Concurrency VII |chapter=In Memoriam: Carl Adam Petri |date=2013|editor-last=Jensen|editor-first=Kurt|editor2-last=van der Aalst|editor2-first=Wil M. P.|editor3-last=Balbo|editor3-first=Gianfranco|editor4-last=Koutny|editor4-first=Maciej|editor5-last=Wolf|editor5-first=Karsten|chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-642-38143-0_1|series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science|volume=7480|language=en|location=Berlin, Heidelberg|publisher=Springer|pages=1–5|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-38143-0_1|isbn=978-3-642-38143-0}}</ref>

Petri started studying mathematics at the Technische Hochschule Hannover (today, the [[Leibniz University Hannover]]) in 1950. He documented Petri nets in 1962 as part of his dissertation, {{lang|de|Kommunikation mit Automaten}} (Communication with automata). From 1959 until 1962 he worked at the [[University of Bonn]] and received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in 1962 from the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]]. From 1963 to 1968, he established and directed the computing centre of [[University of Bonn|Bonn University]].<ref name=":1" /> In 1968, he became head of {{lang|de|Forschungsinstitut für Informationssysteme}} of the newly founded [[Gesellschaft für Mathematik und Datenverarbeitung]] (GMD). He retired in 1991.

In 1988, Petri became honorary professor of the [[University of Hamburg]].<ref>[http://www.informatik.uni-hamburg.de/TGI/mitarbeiter/profs/petri_eng.html Petri's page at the University of Hamburg]</ref> He was a member of the [[Academia Europaea]].

Petri's work significantly advanced the fields of [[parallel computing]] and [[distributed computing]], and it helped define the modern studies of [[complex system]]s and [[workflow management system]]s. His contributions have been in the broader area of [[network theory]], which includes coordination models and theories of interaction, and eventually led to the formal study of software connectors.

==Awards==
Petri was honoured with the following awards:

* 1993: [[Konrad Zuse Medal]] of the [[Gesellschaft für Informatik]].<ref>[http://www.gi.de/?id=276 Konrad-Zuse-Medaille] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140819084001/http://www.gi.de/?id=276 |date=2014-08-19 }}, [[Gesellschaft für Informatik]] (in German), retrieved 2012-03-09.</ref> 
* 1997: [[Werner von Siemens Ring]], a prestigious German award in technical sciences.<ref>[https://idw-online.de/de/news1391] idw - Informationsdienst Wissenschaft (in German), retrieved 2016-02-24.</ref><ref>[http://siemens-ring.de/portfolio_page/carl-adam-petri/] Stiftung Werner-von-Siemens-Ring (in German), retrieved 2016-02-24.</ref>
* 1999: Doctorate ''[[Honoris causa|Honoris Causa]]'' from the [[University of Zaragoza|Universidad de Zaragoza]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Silva|first=Manuel|date=14 October 2013|title=Half a century after Carl Adam Petri's Ph.D. thesis: A perspective on the field|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1367578813000473|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=24 September 2020|journal=Annual Reviews in Control|volume=37|issue=2|pages=191–219|doi=10.1016/j.arcontrol.2013.09.001|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
* 2003: honoured by [[Beatrix of the Netherlands|Her Majesty the Queen of the Netherlands]] with the title ''Commander in the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]]''.<ref name=":0" />
* 2007: honoured for his lifetime achievements by the "Academy of Transdisciplinary Learning and Advanced Studies (ATLAS)" with an "Academy Gold Medal of Honour".<ref>[http://www.theatlas.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=144&Itemid=116] TheATLAS, retrieved 2016-02-24.</ref> 
* 2008: [[Computer Pioneer Award]] from the [[IEEE]] for his inspiration of [[Petri net]]s.<ref>[https://www.computer.org/web/awards/pioneer-carl-petri] Carl Adam Petri, 2008 IEEE Computer Pioneer Award Recipient, retrieved 24 February 2016.</ref><ref name=":0" />
